The political crisis follows the Polish government's push to remove Tribunal judges appointed under the previous PiS administration, which governed from 2015 to 2023. During that period, EU officials accused the court of lacking independence, while its rulings challenging the primacy of EU law angered elites in Brussels. PiS supporters gathered outside the Tribunal on Friday night after its president, Bogdan Święczkowski, was suspended and Judge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska announced that she was assuming leadership. Pro-EU globalist Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk vowed to overhaul the Tribunal, declaring that "in certain matters, there can be no compromise." Tusk defended the overhaul of the court as necessary to restore a weakened tribunal. He said, "There was never any doubt that the court in the form imposed by PiS was not a genuine court."
